transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

I'm here because I have an intense, overwhelming fear of heights that I just can't seem to manage on my own anymore. It has gotten really difficult to deal with, so I decided it was time to seek some professional help.
Can you tell me more about what happens when you're in a situation where you're exposed to heights, such as being on a high floor of a building or looking out from a great height?

The moment I look down from a high place, I get hit with an immediate, overwhelming panic and my body completely freezes up. My heart starts racing incredibly fast, I struggle to breathe, and I begin trembling and sweating uncontrollably.
How long have you been experiencing this intense fear of heights, and did it start suddenly or develop gradually over time?

I have been dealing with this intense fear of heights for about a year and nine months now. As for how it began, I'm not really sure and can't quite remember if it started suddenly or built up gradually.
I'm sorry, I didn't quite catch that last part. Could you please repeat your question for me?
Do you find yourself actively avoiding situations or places that involve heights, such as tall buildings, mountains, or bridges, because of your fear?

Yes, absolutely. I go completely out of my way and take long detours just to avoid crossing bridges or going near tall buildings. I've even had to refuse invitations to social events because the fear of being up high is just too overwhelming.
How has your fear of heights affected your daily life, relationships, and work or school performance over the past year or so?

Over the last year and nine months, it has severely restricted my life. I actually had to turn down a job promotion because the new office was on the 20th floor, and I can't even join my friends at rooftop venues anymore. It has caused a lot of strain because I constantly have to plan my entire day just to avoid any high places.
